claim: You can consume DynamoDB Streams records with AWS Lambda, which is synchronously invoked when new stream records are available (you can subscribe up to two Lambda functions to the same stream), with Apache Flink through Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, and with an Amazon EventBridge pipe, which consumes events from DynamoDB Streams and routes them to a target such as an EventBridge bus.

evidence.quote: When new stream records are available, your Lambda function is synchronously invoked. You can subscribe up to two Lambda functions to the same DynamoDB stream.

| [Ability to consume Amazon DynamoDB Streams records with Apache Flink](#DocumentHistory) | You can now consume Amazon DynamoDB Streams records with Apache Flink and leverage the Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink to quickly build and manage end-to-end stream processing applications. For more information, see [DynamoDB Streams and Apache Flink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/StreamsApacheFlink.html). | November 12, 2024 |

An EventBridge pipe consumes events from DynamoDB Streams and routes them to a target such as an EventBridge bus (an event bus is a router that receives events and delivers them to destinations, also called targets).
